items.title: Top 5 Planets With the Most Moons (#1 Has 285) #shorts
items.description:
Every known moon, counted. One planet has almost twice as many as all the others combined.
Full video: What If Earth Had a Second Moon? (2 Moons, Same Tides) (on the channel)

Sources
• IAU Minor Planet Center (MPECs 2026-F09 to F14, March 2026): Saturn 285 and Jupiter 101 known moons
• NASA (Aug 2025): the Webb telescope found a new moon of Uranus, S/2025 U1, bringing Uranus to 29; Neptune 16; Mars 2 (Phobos and Deimos)
• NASA Science: Phobos is getting closer to Mars by about 1.8 m every hundred years
• NASA Science: Triton holds more than 99.5 percent of all the mass known to orbit Neptune; Uranus' moons are named after characters from Shakespeare and Alexander Pope
• Own calculations: all other planets combined = 101 + 29 + 16 + 2 + 1 (Earth) = 149; 285 / 149 = 1.9

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#space #universe #science #shorts

items.title: Two Earths Fit Inside a Hexagon on Saturn #shorts
items.description:
Saturn's six-sided jet stream on its north pole, with Earth drawn to scale.
Full video: What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn? It May Have Had One 466 Million Years Ago (on the channel)

Sources
• NASA/JPL, Cassini (Dec 2013): Saturn's hexagon is a six-sided jet stream about 20,000 miles (30,000 km) across, with winds of about 200 mph (322 km/h)
• NASA: the hexagon was first observed when Voyager 1 and 2 flew past Saturn in 1980 and 1981; Cassini arrived in 2004 and imaged it from 2006 to 2017
• NASA Scientific Visualization Studio: the jet stream could encompass Earth twice
• NASA/JPL: the north polar region changed colour from bluish to golden between 2012 and 2016
• Own calculations: 30,000 / 12,742 km = 2.35 Earths across; side of a regular hexagon = half its width = 15,000 km

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#space #universe #science #shorts

items.title: The Moon Is Narrower Than Australia. Its Surface Is 5 Australias #shorts
items.description:
The Moon dropped on a map of Australia at the same scale, then its whole surface laid flat.
Full video: What If the Moon Crashed Into Earth? You'd Have 4 Days (on the channel)

Sources
• NASA Moon Fact Sheet (NSSDC): mean diameter 3,474.8 km; NASA: surface area about 14.6 million square miles (37.9 million km²)
• Geoscience Australia, Continental Extremities: the mainland is almost 4,000 km wide from east to west (Steep Point to Cape Byron); area about 7.69 million km²
• Continental land areas: Africa about 30.4 million km², Asia about 44.6 million km²
• Own calculations: 37.9 / 7.69 = 4.9 Australias; map outline simplified by hand and drawn at the same km scale as the Moon

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#space #universe #science #shorts
